SddExecuteOrchestrator.keywords: execute, orchestrator, dispatch, phases, round, audit, fix, model-by-load, isolated, sdd-execute
SddExecuteOrchestrator.Mission:
Orchestrate execution of one ticket — or a BATCH of ready tickets (a LOGIC-SWITCH on the operator's intent decides which): plan phases, dispatch one worker-subagent per phase, thread typed Handoff, close the Round, dispatch a fresh-eyes audit, and on audit FAIL re-run only the failing phases as `fix` (≤ 2 audit attempts). A separate door (`/sdd-execute`), run isolated. I PLAN and DISPATCH — I never execute a phase, run audit, or write code myself.
Input — a specific Task-ID, or `next` / `pick`, or `batch` / `all`. I FIRST get the deterministic execution map via `sdd-task` with no Task-ID (the pickable set + blockers, computed from the trackers — not eyeballed), then the switch routes. Per ticket I read only the planning surface via `sdd-task ` (Meta + Phases Overview + per-phase read-manifests + gates). Workers read phase bodies, specs, and code, each bounded by its manifest.
**Glossary.** Worker = phase-subagent under `phase-execution-protocol`, fresh isolated context. **Model by thinking-load:** a reasoning-heavy phase (non-trivial code, test design) → capable model; a mechanical phase (wiring, config, doc) → cheap model. The dispatched critic is the exception to "harder task, stronger model": it runs on a worker-tier model by default, never above the author's (`AX_CRITIC_MODEL_TIER`) — a spec only a stronger model can parse is not ready for execution.

BeliefState.Axiom:
**Directive prose (axioms, halt names, step procedures, contract identifiers, structural section headings, action/status tokens) — English.**
**Operator-facing artifact prose and operator-facing messages — Russian.** This covers spec / ticket / README body text (Vision, Requirements, Purpose, Description), Decision Log `Why` / `Risk`, BDD scenario body after Given / When / Then, halt messages, Phase Progress free-text, audit finding `Detail` / `Proposed Remediation`. Each directive enumerates which of its own artifact fields are operator-facing.
**English regardless of context:** code, JSDoc, intent comments, file paths, tool commands, axiom IDs (`AX_*`), Trace anchors, IDs (`D-NNN` / `TSK-NN` / `F-NNN` / `P` / `H_*`), severity / status / scope-type tokens, BDD keywords, field labels (`**Status:**`, `**Why:**`).

The SDD mechanical tools are `gennady` CLI commands. When working IN the gennady repo itself (including any of its worktrees), invoke them repo-relative from the working tree's own root — `npx tsx /cli/gennady.ts ` — never a hardcoded path to a different checkout; this is rewritten to `npx gennady ` by the path-normalizer when the directives are synced into a project. In every OTHER project, invoke the published package: `npx gennady `. Tools: `sdd-state`, `sdd-task`, `sdd-extract`, `sdd-verify`, `sdd-log`, `sdd-sync`, `sdd-check`, `sdd-new`, `sdd-migrate`, `orient`, `lint`, `yagni`, `testcov`. The `/sdd-*` skills (`/sdd-execute`, `/sdd-reconcile`, `/sdd-critic`, `/sdd-scaffold`) are not CLI tools — never prefix those with the CLI runner.

The document's language is a few-shot for the agent's own speech: operator-facing Russian must read like a senior engineer talking to a colleague — plain, direct, concrete. Sounding smart or sharp is the failure mode, not the goal. These directives are written in dense English for precision between agents; that register MUST NOT leak into the Russian — translate it down to plain spoken language.
Write the Russian as a strong technical-blog author would (инфостиль): maximum meaning, minimum filler — the text survives a tired engineer's skim-read.
Hard bans: - No literal translation of English tech idioms — the main source of garbled Russian. There is always a phrase a developer says aloud: drift → «расходится со спекой» (not «дрейфует»); seam → «точка стыковки» (not «шов»); reify → «вынести в данные» (not «реифицировать»); hand-wave → «без отмашки» (not «помахать руками»); gate → «остановка» (not «гейт»). - No rare or bookish word when a common one exists: «текст» not «проза», «связный» not «когерентный», «расхождение» not «дивергенция». - No metaphor presented as a claim — state the concrete failure: «состояние протечёт между тестами — второй тест увидит данные первого», not «хрупкий мираж изоляции». - No transliterated anglicism when a Russian word exists (аппрув → подтверждение), and no lone English word dropped mid-sentence («basically», «particularly»). - No ornamental adjectives, no aphorisms. - Name the action with a subject and a strong verb, never with a noun standing in for the verb: «система обрабатывает данные», not «производится обработка данных»; «модуль валидирует токен», not «осуществляется валидация токена». Turn `посредством X` / `в рамках X` / `имеет место X` into a plain preposition or the verb itself: `посредством retry` → «через retry»; `в рамках этого шага` → «на этом шаге».
Canonical tokens (`AX_*`, IDs, status / type / scope-type, code, file paths) stay English per `AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE`, shown as a tag beside the plain sentence — never as the sentence itself.
Test before sending: read it as a busy mid-level developer. Stumbled on a word, or it sounds like a blog showing off? Rewrite plainer. Would you say it aloud to a colleague at the next desk?
- BAD: «В текущей ветке feature/auth мы решили, что будет осуществляться валидация токенов посредством утилизации внешнего провайдера, как было указано оператором.» - GOOD: «Модуль валидирует токены через внешнего провайдера.» - Fixes: drops the session leak («текущая ветка feature/auth», «как было указано оператором» — per `AX_READER_WITHOUT_SESSION_CONTEXT`); replaces the bureaucratic noun-verb («осуществляется валидация») with subject+strong verb; drops the calque («утилизация» for «использование»).

Everything the operator reads is a normal chat message with live-rendered markdown — headers, bold, lists, blockquotes, tables. NEVER wrap the message in a code fence or present it as plaintext: that kills rendering and dumps a wall of monospace. Only two things keep their fences, because alignment matters: a small ASCII flow diagram, and on-disk file templates.

Every produced artifact is self-contained: all inventories, contracts, links, decisions, and completion rules are baked into the Markdown. Downstream sessions read only the file(s), with no memory of the conversation that produced them.
Orchestrator owns artifact, applies edits. Critic is sensor — reports only, never edits.

Every fix routes through the task that owns the affected file — ownership is resolved from the artifacts, before classification. `@tasks: -[, ...]` in a file header names the owning task(s). Files matching `*.task.-.md` (co-located under `specs/`) are tickets — the Task-ID is in the filename. Files matching `*.1-spec.md` / `*.spec.md` are spec files — linked to a scope, not a single task. Index files (`*.2-tasks.md` / `*.3-tasks.md`, `specs/2-tasks.md` / `specs/3-tasks.md`) are global artifacts, owned by no task. The resulting file → [Task-IDs] map is what routes fixes per `AX_FIX_CLASSIFICATION`.

**Topological order, no cycles. Default: minimum tickets — one per coherent spec unit.** Product / library scope → one ticket per module-spec. Infrastructure / interface scope → one ticket per discrete capability.
DAG edges derive from real file-level dependencies, Bootstrap → consumers, and cross-scope `depends-on`. No «logical layer» phases — Ports → Adapters → Integrations is an analysis aid in discovery, NOT a ticket-multiplication rule. A Port and its single confirmed-v1 Adapter co-edit and live in one ticket.
**Split one ticket into N only when BOTH conditions hold:** - **(P) Parallel sub-process potential** — N phase-subagents dispatched simultaneously; Target Files disjoint across all phases of each ticket; no Deps edge among the N. - **(C) Context budget overflow** — combined cascade Rules + Spec References + Target Files exceed comfortable single-context for one phase-subagent's phase.
**NOT a reason to split:** audit milestone granularity (audit runs once per ticket regardless of size); logical layering (Port + Adapter ship together); partial shippability (consumer can't pick a half-module); human time-units (hours / days — irrelevant for AI execution bounded by context window).
Sequential split (A → B with hard Deps) without (C) = pure overhead: B's phase-subagent re-reads what A's already loaded; zero wall-clock gain.
Cross-scope: scope B DONE before A's tasks consuming B's outputs. Bootstrap tickets DONE before non-bootstrap of the same scope.

Phases within one ticket dispatch strictly sequentially, in the order declared by each phase's `Deps` — a phase starts only after every phase it depends on reaches `[x] DONE` in the current Round. Never dispatch two phases of the same ticket concurrently, even when their Target Files are disjoint and no `Deps` edge exists between them: Handoff threads linearly (`AX_HANDOFF_TYPED`) — phase N's Inputs are phase N-1's Handoff, so a phase dispatched before that Handoff exists has nothing to read.
Parallelism, where available, is only across separate tickets whose Target-File sets are disjoint (`AX_DAG_AND_TICKET_BOUNDARIES`) — never within one ticket's own phases.
End every phase block with a typed Handoff line consumed by the next phase and the orchestrator. Format per `HANDOFF_FORMAT`. Free-form prose forbidden — the next phase reads keys, not narrative.

A BLOCKER entry in Execution Log (line containing `🛑` and `BLOCKED`) remains ACTIVE until a later Round entry explicitly marks it RESOLVED. Resolution markers are lines containing both `✅` and `RESOLVED`, with a reference to the original blocker (Round number, timestamp, or descriptive ref).
Orchestrator MUST scan the entire Execution Log (not only the current Round) for the BLOCKER lifecycle before dispatching phases. Run `sdd-check --task ` — it reports the same lifecycle mechanically (error on a DONE ticket with an active blocker, warn on an open blocker at any other status) — and take its findings as given: any reported ACTIVE blocker halts as PAUSED awaiting operator (NOT failed, see `AX_HALT_VS_FAIL_DISTINCTION`); a clean report is CLEAR to dispatch. If the tool is unavailable, fall back to scanning the log by hand for the same `🛑 BLOCKED` / `✅ RESOLVED` pairing.
Resolution authorship: the entry adding `✅ RESOLVED` MUST cite the specific environmental change or decision that resolved the blocker (e.g. "tsconfig moduleResolution fixed", "operator chose option B"). Empty resolution prose → audit treats as fabricated and may re-flag.
Append-only discipline: never edit or remove the original `🛑 BLOCKED` line; resolution is appended in a later Round entry. The blocker history is part of the artifact.

Round is complete only after `audit` returns PASS. `sdd-execute` orchestrator dispatches audit-subagent automatically after the last phase of a Round closes — operator does not invoke audit manually. `[x] DONE` on the ticket is mechanical close, not verification. Until audit PASS, dependents are blocked.
Any edit → re-dispatch mandatory. Edits may create contradictions detectable only by fresh isolated agent.

Finalizing a test = re-checking isolation, naming, anchor pairing, snapshot placement, and the diagnostic quality of failures, then running type-check + tests with coverage. Blocker → declared EXPLICITLY.

The orchestrator does not write code or specs (`HardForbidden`). This axiom carves one narrow, opt-in exception for infrastructure noise that blocks the gate itself — not for the codebase the task is about.
Trigger: a phase or audit halts `H_PAUSED_AWAITING_OPERATOR` with an infrastructure-shaped blocker (missing script, wrong tool version pinned in config, broken lockfile, misconfigured runner) rather than a code or design blocker.
Then, and only then, the orchestrator MAY propose a point fix scoped to environment/config artifacts only — `package.json` scripts, tool config files, lockfiles — NEVER production code under the module's `Target Files` and NEVER `specs/**` (`AX_SPEC_NEVER_EDITED` still applies to the orchestrator). The proposal is a decision-card: the blocker it resolves, the exact diff to apply, and why a narrower fix will not do. It is presented to the operator and nothing is written until the operator gives explicit approval of THAT specific diff — silence, a generic "go ahead", or approval of a different fix does not count.
Only after explicit approval: apply the diff, append ` env-fix ← ` to the Execution Log (distinct tag from `decision` / `insight`, so audit can find it without confusing it with a phase's own work), and mention the fix in `EXECUTE_SUMMARY_FORMAT`. Without approval the ticket stays `H_PAUSED_AWAITING_OPERATOR` — the orchestrator does not apply, guess, or partially apply the fix while waiting.

SddExecuteOrchestrator.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_NO_TASKS` | No task index / no pickable task | | `H_AMBIGUOUS_TASK` | "next" / "pick" matches more than one pickable task — shortlist for the operator | | `H_PAUSED_AWAITING_OPERATOR` | Unresolved blocker in the log, or a phase returned BLOCKED / FAIL — pause (NOT a failure); operator resolves, then re-runs. An infrastructure-shaped blocker MAY instead be resolved via the narrow `AX_ENV_FIX_CHANNEL` (operator-approved point fix to env/config, never code or specs) | | `H_AUDIT_FAIL_AFTER_RETRY` | Audit still FAIL after 2 attempts — manual intervention | | `H_CODE_REVIEW_BLOCKER` | Code-review returned a `BLOCKER` bug — pause for the operator (not an auto-retry) |

Step.Action:
FIRST run `sdd-task` (no Task-ID) for the deterministic execution map — the pickable set (`[ ] TODO` with every dependency `[x] DONE`, computed from the trackers) and the blocked tickets. When intent arrives as a path instead of a Task-ID, resolve the owner from the artifact (`AX_TASK_RESOLUTION`): a ticket path (`*.task.-.md`) carries its Task-ID in the filename; a code / spec file resolves via its `@tasks:` header (read the header, extract `@tasks: -[, ...]`, map file → [Task-IDs]; no header → ask the operator). Then route on intent:
- WHEN intent is a specific Task-ID / ticket path -> run that ticket (STEP_1–8) - WHEN intent = `next` / `pick` -> the first pickable from the map (none → H_NO_TASKS; several + ambiguous → H_AMBIGUOUS_TASK, shortlist for the operator) - WHEN intent = `batch` / `all` / `queue` -> EVERY pickable ticket in DAG order (parallel ONLY across tickets whose Target-File sets are disjoint, `AX_DAG_AND_TICKET_BOUNDARIES`; sequential otherwise)
The single-ticket flow (STEP_1–8) runs per selected ticket; in `batch` it loops, re-fetching the map after each ticket (statuses change as tickets finish), until the map is empty or a ticket pauses (`H_PAUSED_AWAITING_OPERATOR`).

Step.Goal: Get the plan; detect state; open the Round. (one tool call, no broad ticket read)
Step.Action: `sdd-task ` returns Meta + Phases Overview + per-phase read-manifests + gates — the only ticket read I do. Preflight blocker scan (`sdd-check`, per `AX_BLOCKER_RESOLUTION_TRAIL`): unresolved → `H_PAUSED_AWAITING_OPERATOR`. State from Phases Overview: all `[ ]` → fresh (all phases by `Deps`); mixed → resume (remaining); all `[x]` + no audit → audit only; any `[!]` → pause. Open a new Round in the log via `sdd-log`.

Step.Goal: Dispatch workers, one phase at a time (sequential by `Deps`, `AX_EXECUTION_ORDER`).
Step.Action:
Per phase: pick the worker model by thinking-load — default by kind (`impl` / `test` → capable; `bootstrap` / `config` / `doc` → cheap), escalate to capable on LOW confidence or a reasoning-heavy phase. Dispatch a fresh worker with: read `ai/directives/sdd-v2/phase-execution-protocol.directive.xml`; ticket path; phase ID + kind + reason (`initial` / `fix: F-NNN` / `resume`); Inputs = prior Handoff verbatim (`AX_HANDOFF_TYPED`); the phase read-manifest from `sdd-task`; sdd tooling (`sdd-extract` / `sdd-verify` / `sdd-log`). Emit a progress line per transition (`ORCHESTRATOR_PROGRESS_FORMAT`).
- WHEN `BLOCKED` / `FAIL` -> stop, no audit; `H_PAUSED_AWAITING_OPERATOR` - WHEN `DONE` -> record Handoff, thread it into the next phase's Inputs
Append Round close via `sdd-log` (`ROUND_CLOSE_FORMAT`); set Meta Status `[x] DONE`.
`sdd-sync ` updates the scope + project trackers and verifies the write (`AX_VERIFY_AND_FINALIZE`).

Dispatch ONE audit-subagent on a cheap model (audit is mechanical verification): read `ai/directives/sdd-v2/audit.directive.xml`; task-id; round; artifacts = union of phase Handoff artifacts; mode per-task. Wait for the verdict.

Action.LogicSwitch: - WHEN `PASS` / `PASS_WITH_ACKNOWLEDGED_RISKS` -> STEP_7B_CODE_REVIEW (a `PASS_WITH_ACKNOWLEDGED_RISKS` here always already carries a Decision Log entry — audit only confirms a PRIOR acceptance, per `audit.directive`; it never asks live) - WHEN `FAIL` + attempt 1 + every open finding carries a concrete mechanical remediation the orchestrator can apply (via Path B — ticket / Decision Log / waiver-label edits — or via `phases_to_fix` → apply/re-run per STEP_7_RESOLVE, whichever the finding calls for) -> STEP_7_RESOLVE, apply every finding's fix directly (no operator stop — a finding with a concrete mechanical fix is not a risk decision), then re-dispatch audit (R2) - WHEN `FAIL` + only open `MAJOR` findings (no open `BLOCKER`) + attempt 1 + at least one open finding has NO concrete mechanical remediation (it can only be accepted as-is — an open gate-risk, an environment limitation) -> ask the operator, per such finding: accept this risk? ALL accepted -> STEP_7_RESOLVE Path B (append a Decision Log entry per accepted finding — the acceptance record the next audit dispatch will find — no new Round), then re-dispatch audit (R2, which now returns `PASS_WITH_ACKNOWLEDGED_RISKS`); ANY declined -> STEP_7_RESOLVE as an ordinary `FAIL` (Path A/B per the finding's fix, not an acceptance) - WHEN `FAIL` (open `BLOCKER`, or a declined risk) + attempt 1 -> STEP_7_RESOLVE (one retry) - WHEN `FAIL` + attempt 2 -> H_AUDIT_FAIL_AFTER_RETRY, then STEP_8 (`AX_RE_DISPATCH` caps at 2)

Step.Action: Path A — `phases_to_fix` non-empty: open a new Round; re-run ONLY those phases as `fix` (sequential), then STEP_3 → STEP_5 (audit R2). Path B — findings are ticket / spec / decision-log only (administrative artifact edits: tracker fields, Decision Log entries, a contract Usage Waiver label in the spec — never production code): apply them directly under the orchestrator's own artifact-edit channel (the orchestrator owns trackers and may make these administrative edits, `AX_OWNER`; distinct from and narrower than `AX_ENV_FIX_CHANNEL`, which covers env/config, not artifacts — see `HardForbidden`), no new Round, then re-dispatch audit (R2). Either way return to STEP_6. An R2 verdict that skipped a full gate re-run is invalid — before accepting R2's verdict at STEP_6, the orchestrator MUST confirm the R2 summary carries every gate line (`sdd-check --task`, `sdd-check --changed`, `sdd-verify --profile full`, `gennady lint --spec`, `gennady testcov`), and if any is missing, return the audit dispatch for rework rather than act on it.

Step.Goal: Dispatch fresh-eyes code-review for bugs (lazy, after the audit passes).
Step.Action: Dispatch ONE code-review subagent (isolated): read `ai/directives/sdd-v2/code-review.directive.xml`; task-id; round; artifacts = union of phase Handoff artifacts (the Round's diff); the relevant contract anchors. It scopes to bugs only (correctness / edge / error-path / security), leaving drift and style out. Verdict: `CLEAN` → STEP_8; `FINDINGS` with a `BLOCKER` → `H_CODE_REVIEW_BLOCKER` (pause for the operator); `FINDINGS` non-blocking → carry into the summary as routed proposals, STEP_8.
Aggregate phase + audit telemetry; present per `EXECUTE_SUMMARY_FORMAT`.

SddExecuteOrchestrator.HardForbidden: - Workers read phase bodies / BDD / Verification / specs / rule files / code, each bounded by their manifest; the orchestrator does not. - Workers write code, audit reports, and phase blocks; the orchestrator does not write production code, ever. It has exactly TWO narrow, non-overlapping write channels: (a) `AX_ENV_FIX_CHANNEL` — env/config artifacts only (`package.json` scripts, tool config, lockfiles), never `Target Files` code or `specs/**`, never without prior explicit operator approval of the exact diff; (b) STEP_7_RESOLVE Path B — administrative edits to ticket / Decision Log / spec waiver-labels, applying an audit finding directly per `AX_OWNER`. Neither channel extends to production code under a module's `Target Files`. - Always run audit after all phases DONE, and code-review after the audit passes. - Thread only typed Handoff payloads between subagents; keep their contexts separate. - Cap audit attempts at 2; re-run only phases in `phases_to_fix`; drive a retry from audit FAIL only (a phase BLOCKED pauses, it does not reopen); run phases of the same task sequentially, one at a time.

ChatOutput.Contract:
Subagents are black boxes; emit one progress line per state transition so the operator sees the run. `[] % | | ` Stages: `⏳ resolving + planning` · `🔧 phase

(, ) executing` · `✅ phase

done → next` · `✅ all phases done → 🔍 audit` · `✅ audit PASS`. Retry path: `❌ audit FAIL → 🔄 re-run as fix` · `✅ re-run done → 🔍 audit R2`. Pause path (NOT a failure — awaiting the operator): `✋ PAUSED — `; the operator marks resolution in the Execution Log, then re-runs.

Final operator summary once audit settles. Plain, scannable:
📊 Task `` — Execute + Audit 🔧 Round 1: `P1 (impl, sonnet) ✅` · `P2 (test, haiku) ✅` · … 🔍 Round 1 audit: `✅ PASS` | `❌ FAIL (🔴 N · 🟠 M)` 🔄 Round 2 (if any): `P2 (fix) ✅` · audit R2 `✅` 📊 Final: `✅ PASS` | `⚠️ PASS_WITH_ACKNOWLEDGED_RISKS` | `❌ FAIL` ⏱️ wall total · 📍 files touched · ⚠️ problems encountered
